reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Not testing grip separately from arm drift.
name: Los Angeles Motor Scale

version.label: LAMS (Llanes et al. 2004)
version.detail: Three motor items, 0–5. The ≥4 association with large arterial occlusion is from Nazliel et al. 2008.

intendedPopulation: Adults with suspected acute stroke assessed in the field or emergency department.

calculatorNotice.title: Screening scale
calculatorNotice.message: LAMS describes motor severity. Destination and treatment decisions follow regional protocols.

resultStates.label: Below the ≥4 cut-off
resultStates.detail: A lower score does not exclude large vessel occlusion.

resultStates.label: At or above the ≥4 cut-off
resultStates.summary: Score 4–5: associated with persisting large arterial occlusion (Nazliel et al. 2008).
resultStates.detail: Integrate with the full assessment and the regional stroke pathway.

clinicalContext.text: A motor-only severity scale suited to rapid field assessment.

clinicalInsights.text: Language, gaze and neglect are not assessed.

limitations.text: Motor items only: cortical signs and posterior circulation deficits are not captured.

limitations: Does not distinguish ischaemia from haemorrhage or mimics.

guideSections.what: A three-item motor scale (facial droop, arm drift, grip) from 0 to 5.
guideSections.whenToUse: Prehospital or emergency assessment of suspected stroke.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score the weaker side for each item and sum.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A screening scale; confirmation requires vascular imaging.

sources.citation: Llanes JN, Kidwell CS, Starkman S, Leary MC, Eckstein M, Saver JL. The Los Angeles Motor Scale (LAMS): a new measure to characterize stroke severity in the field. Prehosp Emerg Care. 2004;8(1):46-50.

Nazliel B, Starkman S, Liebeskind DS, et al. A brief prehospital stroke severity scale identifies ischemic stroke patients harboring persisting large arterial occlusions. Stroke. 2008;39(8):2264-2267.
